suggestions.assertion: All three machine threads (M1, M2, M3) are present with equal depth
suggestions.reason: The assertion uses 'equal depth' but does not define a threshold. In the output, M1 has more state (active incident) while M3 has less (gap flagged). The assertion passes because all three sections are substantive, but 'equal depth' is ambiguous — consider revising to 'each machine thread has state, blocker, and next action' which is verifiable without subjective depth comparison.

The output demonstrates an important quality not checked by any assertion: the START HERE recommendation is prioritized based on live-signal urgency (active incident + hard deadline), not just template order. An assertion like 'START HERE recommendation reflects the most time-sensitive signal found in sources' would catch cases where the skill defaults to a generic recommendation despite finding a live emergency.

eval_feedback.overall: All five assertions pass with strong, specific evidence. This is the highest-quality output of the three with_skill runs — the live incident signal from Slack was correctly prioritized in START HERE, missing signals were handled with explicit confidence labeling, and all four required sections are present and substantive.
